subject: KiteWave procurement path — invoice acceptance and card limits
body:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@kitewave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22 09:12 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: procurement path & payment constraints (post-demo)

Hi Samira — great to meet you and Daniel this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- What we heard: KiteWave is interested in a Q1 pilot using Redwood for inference on your internal analytics models. Procurement prefers paper-based PO for production contracts but is open to card for short pilots (under finance thresholds).
- Open questions we flagged on the call: vendor onboarding lead time, AP requirements for tax forms/insurance, and card single-transaction caps for pilot runs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I attach our standard SOW template + vendor onboarding checklist for your procurement team to review.
2) Can you confirm the contact at procurement who owns vendor setup and the PO process? (we can send the checklist directly).
3) Karthik will follow up with a proposed pilot commercial path (card trial vs short-term invoice) based on the thresholds you confirm.

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template.pdf; Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

— Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- Production purchases above our delegated authority require a formal PO and 30-45 day net payment terms.
- For pilots under $15k, procurement allows use of corporate card; there is an approval flow but typically faster (3–5 business days).
- Vendor onboarding commonly requires W-9/COI, bank remittance info, and a brief security attestation for hosted services.

I'll introduce our procurement lead in a separate email — that person handles vendor set-up and will confirm whether KiteWave would prefer to pilot on card or proceed with a PO.

Also looping in Daniel who had a note on contract term length for pilots (he prefers month-to-month initially).

Best,
Samira

Thanks Samira — helpful. A couple operational notes from our side so procurement has everything they need to decide quickly: 

- If KiteWave decides to pilot on card, we can do a short-term invoice for the same amount if you prefer — we are flexible. For pilots under $15k, card is simplest and keeps procurement lead time minimal.
- If procurement requires a PO, we can accept a PO that references the SOW and issue invoices monthly net-30.
- Ben, can you confirm whether Redwood Finance needs supplier tax/insurance forms before sending the first invoice for a PO? Also what is our vendor enrollment SLA for new customers?

Samira — once you share the procurement contact, we can route the checklist and SOW directly.

Quick finance notes: 

- Required before first invoice (PO path): signed SOW, completed W-9, Certificate of Insurance (COI), and bank remittance details.
- Vendor onboarding SLA: typical turnaround is 7–12 business days after we have completed vendor paperwork (depends on back-and-forth with procurement).
- Thresholds: corporate card transactions are limited to $15,000 per invoice by default; exceptions possible but require manager approval and audit trail.
- For production contracts >$50k annually, our standard procurement practice is to request a PO and set up annual invoicing cadence (monthly or net-30) per the SOW.

I can expedite COI requests if procurement needs an insurer contact — happy to engage.

— Ben

Thanks all — summary and mutual action plan:

- KiteWave procurement contact: Samira to introduce procurement lead (procurement@kitewave.com).
- If procurement confirms card for pilot: target pilot spend <= $15k, Redwood to provide invoice option and card payment instructions; procurement to confirm approval SLA.
- If procurement requires PO: KiteWave to share PO template, procurement to return signed SOW + W-9 + COI + remittance info; Redwood Finance to issue monthly invoices net-30. Vendor onboarding ~7–12 business days.
- Pilot commercial path decision due: 2026-11-29 (end of next week).
- Action owners: Samira (introduce procurement lead), Procurement (confirm card vs PO and share any vendor form templates), Karthik (prepare pilot commercial summary and sample invoice), Ben (standby to receive vendor paperwork and expedite COI).

Can we book a 30-min slot for Tuesday 11/30 to lock the commercial path once procurement confirms? Proposed time: 10:30am PT. If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.
